passage:
At five, Akash sat down ten minutes after starting his blocks. "I'm bored. Can I watch a video?" Papa Shankar sat him at the table with an empty egg carton, some paper strips and a glue stick. Akash sighed, then began turning the carton into a caterpillar with long paper legs.
At nine, Akash was in the last period of a hot afternoon when Jahnavi Ma'am began reading the next chapter aloud in a flat, even voice. Akash slumped in his seat. "She doesn't care about this lesson," he whispered to himself. "She sounds so bored." By the end of the reading, he had almost stopped listening. At the bell, Jahnavi Ma'am rubbed her eyes and smiled tiredly at the class. "Sorry, everyone. Today was a long day with the parent meetings. Did you follow the chapter?" Akash blinked. She had been tired, and her flat voice had said nothing about how she felt about the lesson. He put up his hand. "I did, but can you say the second paragraph again?" She nodded and read it again, a little slower.

qa.q: What did Papa Shankar give Akash to use instead of a video?
qa.a: He gave him an empty egg carton, some paper strips and a glue stick.

qa.q: How do Akash's boredom at five and his guess about Jahnavi Ma'am's voice at nine show two sides of boredom?
qa.a: At five Akash said he was bored, and with an egg carton, paper strips and glue he made a caterpillar. At nine he thought Jahnavi Ma'am sounded so bored and did not care about the lesson, but her flat voice came from a long day, so a flat tone does not say how she feels about it.

qa.q: What was Akash thinking when he whispered that Jahnavi Ma'am sounded so bored?
qa.a: He thought she did not care about the lesson, and he felt let down and lost interest.

qa.q: What could Akash do when a teacher's flat voice makes him feel she does not care?
qa.a: He can wait to see the whole context and ask kindly, as he did by asking her to repeat the paragraph.

grounding: A child's own boredom becoming imagination (4068) and, later, hearing a flat voice as boredom when it means tiredness (2371): one boy across years.
